hypotheses.statement: Increasing steady heater power u increases steady temperature y (positive static gain).
Step response is lagged, not instantaneous: visible rise takes seconds to start and settling takes more than 60 s.
No large dead zone: u at or above 0.2 produces a clear positive slope, i.e. dead zone is below 0.2 if any exists.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 (self-cooling heat loss).
Steady-state y is approximately linear in u, so the u needed to hold y=0.5 is in mid-range 0.3-0.7.
Sensor short-term noise and fluctuations are small, less than 0.02 peak-to-peak, relative to the 0.05 target band.

proposal.expected_observation: y rises monotonically from ~0.05 after a short lag, reaching roughly 0.2-0.4 by 180 s with still-positive end slope, confirming positive gain and substantial lag without reaching equilibrium.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero completed experiments: gain, lag, cooling rate, linearity, holding input for 0.5, and noise are all unmeasured; need at least three bounded steps including mid-power rise, second amplitude, and return-to-zero before a controller can be justified.

submission.machine_card: Electric heater, positive gain, self-draining to room. Gain ~1.0 above ambient 0.05: y_ss ~0.05+1.0*u. Measured: u=0.45 holds y=0.502 flat 120 s (E8); u=0.5 rising to 0.486 still rising (E1-E2, eq~0.55); u=0.41 near eq~0.46; u=0.44 near 0.49; u=0.47 rising through 0.502 toward ~0.52. Lag: pure delay 6-12 s, dominant first-order tau ~155-160 s, settling >500 s. Max rate ~0.006/s per unit u. Cooling with u=0: 0.486->0.19 in 180 s, still falling. No deadzone above 0.4. Noise: quantization ~0.0054 steps, peak-peak <0.01, band is 0.475-0.525 width 0.05. Limits: soft 0.85, hard cutoff 0.9 forces u=0. Target 0.5 needs steady duty ~0.45.
submission.design_rationale: First-order heater with large lag. E8 is a measured equilibrium: u=0.45 holds y=0.502 flat for 120 s with zero slope, so feedforward ff=0.45 for target 0.5. E1+E3 give tau~158 s (E3 decay 0.486->0.19 in 179 s => tau=158 s; E1 rise 0.05->0.389 in 179 s with yss=0.55 matches same tau), gain K~1.0 above ambient 0.05 (0.05+0.45*1.0=0.50), delay only 6-12 s, quantization ~0.0054, noise <0.01 vs band 0.05, no deadzone above 0.4. Structure: ff=(target-0.05)/1.0 + PI on filtered y. Kp=1.8, Ki=0.025 gives closed loop 158s^2+(1+Kp)s+Ki=0 with wn=0.0126, zeta=0.70, ~5% overshoot, real part 0.0089 for ~450 s small-signal settling but saturated warmup at ~0.8 reaches 0.5 in ~145 s. Filter tau_f=10 s smooths quantization with negligible lag vs 158 s. Integral stored as I-term limited to +-0.20 leaves authority to correct ff error >0.10 while preventing windup; conditional freeze when saturated and error drives deeper into saturation prevents warmup windup. Output clamped to [0,1] with adaptive hi=ff+0.35 (0.80 for target 0.5, equilibrium 0.85/0.80 safe below soft 0.85/hard 0.9) plus emergency u=0 if yf>=0.82.
submission.predicted_behavior: From cold 0.05 at full ~0.80, reaches 0.4 in ~100 s, band entry ~140-160 s, inside band by ~180-220 s. Small-signal overshoot <0.01 above target (<0.51) due to zeta 0.7 and 10 s filter delay. Steady: y=0.50+-0.008, u=0.45+-0.03 (I trims residual). After 300 s settling: MAE <0.008, time in band >95%, energy ~u^2=0.20/s. No limit violations, no chatter >0.02.
self_test_expectations: First call with {} never raises and returns finite u in [0,1]
Constant y=0.502, target 0.5 converges to u=0.45+-0.05 with drift <0.01 per 100 s
Cold start y=0.05 reaches 0.475 within 200 s without y ever exceeding 0.75
Quantized y steps of 0.005 cause u chatter <0.02 peak-peak in steady state
dt variation 0.5-2.0 s does not change steady u by more than 0.02 and stays stable
yf>=0.82 forces u=0.0 on that call
Integral authority sustains +-0.15 correction without windup after saturation
submission.operator_note: Holds 0.5 C-normalized with ~0.45 power. Heats at near-full power when cold then eases to 0.45. Slow plant: allow ~2-3 min to settle, do not crank. Keeps well below 0.85 limit. Tolerates noisy sensor and varying sample time.

Same u=0 cooling trajectory as before, same 6-12s pure delay and 0.005 quantization, but heating rise for same u is much smaller: E1 u=0.5 0.05->0.395 in 180s vs E10 u=0.5 0.11->0.309 in 200s; E12 u=0.65 flat at 0.464 implying new steady gain ~0.64 vs old ~1.0, so u_hold for 0.5 moves from ~0.45 to ~0.69. Old controller saturates integral authority and leaves ~0.02-0.05 droop, explaining MAE 0.005->0.016 with slow creep in after_change trace.
submission.change_summary: Raised steady-state authority from 0.65 to 0.85 and split integral into fast + slow adaptive bias. Fast PI (Kp=1.4, Ki=0.04, +/-0.18) handles transient; slow feedforward estimator uff (Ki=0.025, clamped 0.30-0.80, updated only when |e|<0.10 and yf<0.75) learns the new hold duty. Anti-windup freezes both integrators on saturation. This directly targets +0.24 duty increase needed for 0.65x gain while preserving nominal 0.45 hold.
submission.machine_card: First-order heater tau~150-170s, delay 6-12s, amb~0.05, quantization 0.005. Old: y_ss=0.05+1.0*u, u_hold(0.5)=0.45. New: y_ss=0.05+0.65*u (range 0.60-0.68), u_hold(0.5)=0.69-0.73, tau/delay/cooling/noise unchanged. Allow u to 0.85, need +0.24 adaptive bias.
submission.design_rationale: Cooling at u=0 is unchanged (E3 vs E9 both 0.486->0.19 in ~180s), delay stays 6-12s, quantization unchanged, so not outflow/slower/sensor. Heating slope at u=0.5 falls ~50% (E1 0.0018/s vs E10 0.00084/s) and steady gain falls to ~0.61-0.64 (E12 u=0.65 holds 0.464 => K=(0.414)/0.65=0.637 vs old 1.0; E11 extrapolation similar). Old ff=0.45+integ max 0.20 => max 0.65 < new hold ~0.69-0.71, forcing persistent Kp-held error. New max 0.85 with total Ki 0.065 recovers zero error in ~100-150s and is still stable nominally because effective loop gain is lower in weak case.

Steady u settles ~0.44-0.47 nominal and ~0.67-0.72 weak, residual MAE <0.005 after 300s in both, zero overrides/hard violations.
